Definition: from G1223 and G236; to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to conciliate:--reconcile.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to be reconciled, to make peace where there was enmity, and it stands in the Sermon on the Mount. The form in the text is the middle voice of the same verb, and the command is plain: first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe reconciliation comes before worship; God will not take my gift while my brother and I are at odds, and the altar can wait until the relationship is mended.
